[i]Why not make some Pizza Dough while you idle[/i] [h1]Ingredients[/h1] [list] [*] 5 cups all purpose (or 00 flour ) + some for dusting [*] 1.5 tsp. instant dry yeast (or active dry yeast) [*] 1.5 tsp. salt [*] 2.25 cups cold water [*] 1 Tb. extra virgin olive oil[/list] [h1]Instructions[/h1] [olist] [*] Place pizza stone in oven and preheat oven as high as it will go for 45 min - 1 hour [*] Add ingredients (flour, salt and yeast) to the bowl of your mixer and mix using the paddle attachment on low speed until all is incorporated, then add cold water [*] Switch to dough hook attachment and mix together on low speed for 8 - 10 min (the dough should be smooth and sticky but should not stick to the sides of the bowl) [*] Once complete, remove the dough from the mixer and cut it into 6 pieces, forming them into balls. Place them on a lightly oiled sheet and drizzle with 1 Tb. of extra virgin olive oil. Cover with plastic wrap and sit at room temperature to rise for 2 hours [*] Sprinkle the counter with flour, take one piece of dough and press down on it with your fingers until you have 1/2" thick circle or oval. Using your fists and knuckles start stretching the dough until 10" in diameter, making sure not to tear it [*] Dust your pizza peel well with semolina flour / corn meal and set your pizza dough on it, making sure it slides easily when moved. Pour 2 - 3 Tb. the pizza sauce in the center and spread it around with the back of a spoon, leaving 1 inch of space at the edges, making sure not to get any on the peel. Sprinkle with the mozzarella and add your favourite toppings. [*] Slide the pie on the preheated pizza stone in a hot 525"F (275"C) degree oven and bake for 5 - 7 minutes or until golden brown on the edges. [*] Remove from the oven and sprinkle with basil and freshly grated parmigiano reggianno. Allow to rest for a few minutes for the cheese to set. [b] Note [/b] [list] [*] If the dough sticks to the sides of your mixer bowl, sprinkle in a little flour. If it's too dry then add a bit more water [*] Make sure to preheat your oven with the pizza stone in it for at least 45 minutes, and finish cooking the pizza under the broiler for a nice charred touch. [*] If topping with heirloom tomato slices, make sure they are firm, otherwise the pizza would be watery.[/list]

Pros -It's Pizza! Everyone loves pizza. -Better new player friendly features which is not exist at Vampire Survivor (VS), our beloved Bullet-hell-Roguelike genre. (Revive is exist as a default without upgrade, Stand still makes magnet effect, Companion which magnet items slowly) Cons -Every single thing that I've never mentioned at Pros section. This game is shxt, even I've got this game free. First, Why the heck boss reward spawned Far Far outside of screen? Second, Why the Fxcking reward has a countdown(30 sec) to disappear? This shxtty feature makes uncomfortable and impossible to take when 2 or more reward spawned simultaneously. In my case (and happened almost every time I played), I take down 2 bosses at the same time, 1 reward (Tomato Tin Can) spawned at the South of screen at the same time the other one spawned North of screen. When I take one, the other one's countdown shows 10 sec remain. Even I upgraded movement speed feature Max level, finally I got both reward at the last tick of countdown 0 sec. Also other case, there's arena somewhere on stage. When you enter arena, you cannot get out until portal destroyed. In that case, you take down bosses far quicker than portal, you cannot receive reward because of you are locked in arena area, countdown ticking to 0. What the heck are you thinking at this, dev? Why you guys makes players uncomfortable and angry? Third, after few minutes game design is very boring. Fourth, dumb graphics. There's no great synergies like VS between many items. Which makes gameplay is simple and quickly getting tired of playing. And effects is bad which has meh graphics, not attractive. But magnetized item has weird moving effect which I cannot distinguish with enemies bullet and feel dizzy. Fifth, game balance is gone. (Not user friendly way) Similar with former Cons. (And as a notice, I got bored to play and collect coins, so I used cheat to got all upgrade and see how different.) I hardly cleared second stage even I've cheated. Which requires Ten Thousands of gold coins and I cannot being OPed. I think VS-like games should be like Trance (Steady to stack-up powers and after that, tremendous powers and effect overwhelm enemies and player feels high great). This game is not that way. You've upgrade? So what? You're just a Pizza, glass-like weak, delicious meal for enemies. This is Bullet-hell VS-like game not Lovecraft (You are feeble, weak, pity creature wait to die) Finally, you cannot manual aim. (Just like Brotato) (And there's still lot more Cons but I don't want to use more time to write.) Your attacks goes to nearest enemy from you. Which you need to get close which is danger and impossible to precisely aim particular enemies you are looking at, when lots of enemies come after you. This feature makes when you are in arena, you're hard to get out even countdown ticking. There's many more bad things (Bad tutorials, No windowed mode, Only sound option exist, Paused at background or using extra screen, MX even this quality ?, etc.) I don't understand this game worth paid price even a single buck. I seriously tired of this kind of Indie devs.

Pros: 1. Cute, novel theme 2. Free, so far. Cons: 1. The "difficulty" of this game feels artificial, it comes largely from screen clutter. Huge amount of projectiles (both from the player and monsters), experience shards, monsters, all in somewhat the same color scheme, sometimes blinking/flashing. Player projectiles also generally do f*** all damage so the monsters really accumulate. 2. Lazy and bad implementation of "pixel art" style, related to Con 1. 3. Game is really inconsistent about amount of information provided. Most times it's extremely vague (e.g. "increase damage a little bit"), a few times it's specific and even gives you specific numbers. 4. It is really incredibly f***ing stupid that some player projectiles sometimes knock enemies "back"... except if the monster is between the player and where the projectile landed, it just pushes monster into you at the speed of light. 5. Many of the meta-progression skills are so dumb. 3% damage here 2% movement speed there. Are you serious? Is this a game or a job? 6. Music volume remains really loud (relative to other programs) even when set to almost 0. SFX can only be toggled on/off, no adjustable volume.

At the moment, Pizza Hero feels like an extremely mid Vampire Survivor's knock off. Don't get it twisted, I have no issue with games that take heavy inspiration from others. As long as the game has a different vibe compared to what it is copying, I can look past the comparisons. However, there are several issues that keep me from completely liking this game: - There are only 4 stages and 3 of them all just blend together, not helped by the fact that they share most of their enemies. - The soundtrack is extremely forgettable. There are only 3-4 songs and none of them stick out in the slightest. - There is no minimap, so most of the time, you are either stuck wandering around or camping out in one location - The vending machines are a neat idea, but they only provide two unique power-ups, none of which feel special - There are very noticeable moments of lag and textures/enemies clipping in and out of existence I still think that this game could become better in the future with some more updates. But as of right now, there is no reason to play this over Vampire Survivors. It costs money, but its extremely cheap, has around a dozen unique characters, stages, a bopping soundtrack, and several impressive DLC packs.

[h3]Pizza Hero is just boring[/h3] Sure, the only bullet heaven I played was well known Vampire Survivors but I assure you: In this one you'll be falling asleep. Progression is just too slow. In my 3 runs (I refused to just give up after one run) I didn't feel like I'm becoming god at all. That’s kinda sad. Art style in unique and in second location it reminded me of a game I loved as a kid (Twin Bee). Just for that alone I’d hope devs would leave alone that one small bug making enemies flicker when you have pineapple I think. Personally it gave more charm to the game. OH and do not believe “controller not supported”. It works just fine. I have no idea why it’s marked this way. Last thing I wanna mention is…. Item drops? Why are they here? You get one pizza item every 30 mins to your inventory. They serve no purpose in game and they aren’t emoticon or anything like that. The only thing you CAN do is sell it. Is this like another Banana game? All in all some says this is a good starter to bullet heaven genre. I’d say it’s isn’t. If this was my first game from whole genre I’d just pass by all the rest. Just way too boring. So I’m glad I could try it out before it became Pay to Play game. It’ll be really depressing if I’d paid for this.

Base gameplay loop gets a tad bit too repetitive after the first hour or so. The side objectives (finding animal cages, finding pizza ovens, and the small arena challenges) are a nice distraction, but they are too few and far between. Would be nice for there to be more side objectives, as well as having more variation between them (an escort mission or an area where you can't dodge for a certain amount of time while something is being finished). Though not a detraction, having a mini-map of some kind might be an idea worth investigating. Once you reach the endgame and have completed all the stages, the game only offers achievements as a form of replayability, and some of these do not respect your time. There are some that require you to reach Wave 100 on each map, which is a very tall order to ask. I've only done one of those. Once your Pizza (the character) has their full build, you can basically just sit in place and not touch the keyboard while the game continues to play itself. However, you can't actually treat it as an idle game, as even if you are full build and can kill all enemies on screen without doing anything, you still need to manually select an upgrade whenever your character levels up.

TLDR: There's some interesting ideas here, but it just doesn't work as a cohesive whole. This pizza is, unfortunately, only half-baked. One of the most glaring examples is picking up coins and gems. After you've spent a set amount of time standing still, the game activates a vacuum effect that sucks up all coins and gems in a set radius, one that's (in my case) just slightly larger than the screen. It's a neat idea, especially as the game heavily discourages standing still, and has multiple mechanics to keep the player moving around. It almost makes moments of 'rest' feel like an earned reward, when you get ahead of the difficulty curve. In a vacuum, this sounds like a pretty good mechanical choice, right? The game has companion pets that follow you around, and automatically pick up gems and/or coins. Most of them have different stats, with variable speed, range, whether they pick up one or both resources, etc. You start each stage with one, and can find more as the stage goes on. In a vacuum, this sounds like a pretty good mechanic, right? The problem is that both of these mechanics compete with one another for utility, and, at least in my experience, the standing still vacuum almost never picks anything up, because the pet(s) have already collected all the nearby gems, and it has a very limited range. There's also a passive item which increases your pizza's personal coin/gem attraction range which is competing with both of the above mechanics, and largely rendered moot. Especially since you only have four passive slots to work with. As another example, the closest equivalent to 'weapon evolutions' from other games in the Garliclike genre is the pizza recipes. These require specific combinations of multiple active and passive items to activate, and you seem to only be able to complete one per run. They also need to be unlocked first, before you can even use them. The intended method of this was by finding the recipes in 'golden cans' which rarely drop from bosses, but after ten hours of play, I have yet to have a golden can drop. Thankfully, they recently updated the game to add a 'daily recipe' mechanic, which allows you to unlock a specific recipe each day, viewable on the title screen. You just need to complete today's recipe in-game, and it'll be unlocked and added to your recipe list. The problem is that you can ONLY view today's recipe on the title screen. If you need to double-check it in-game, you need to have either written it down first, or look it up in a guide. Outside of this, there are also a lot of small issues that sully the experience, like enemies that blend into the background, a very slow grind on meta-progression, or wonky hitboxes. That's not to say the game doesn't do anything right! As mentioned with the pets, and treating 'getting to stay still' as a reward, it has a lot of interesting mechanics! But the overall experience just doesn't quite come together as well as other games in the genre.

[h1][b] TLDR: A Vampire Survivors knockoff that copies the formula but forgot the fun. Clunky skills, terrible audio, and poor graphics/UI, make this feel like a 48-hour game jam project. [/b] [/h1] [h1]PROS: [/h1] ➕Decent (Vampire) Survivors-like mechanics [h1]NEUTRALS: [/h1] 🔹Like the pizza theme, but I’d like to see more pizza-themed levels instead of Survivors levels [h1]CONS: [/h1] ➖Feels cheap/clunky ➖Graphic settings don’t save - game is forced into full screen every time upon opening ➖Poor sound effects ➖Severe lack of sustain turns runs into more of a bullet hell instead of a Survivor-like [h1] [b] Content (Game world/Narrative) – [3/10] [/b] [/h1] The game world has a few different areas, like a graveyard and a forest. The levels seem infinite, similar to Vampire Survivors. Nothing too special here, but I do appreciate more attention on the levels than say Brotato. No narrative. [h1][b] Gameplay (Mechanics/Difficulty) – [3/10] [/b] [/h1] The mechanics here are pretty much a Survivor’s-like game that borrows heavily from Vampire Survivors (VS), with some slight differences. The biggest being obviously the entire game is pizza themed. Each topping does their own attack, but otherwise, it’s the same as VS - just with black olives instead of bibles. There is a pet system. You can find and unlock pets which help you pick up EXP. There’s also a dodge too. You can jet forward a little bit to better reposition. Nothing much else seems to be different though. I’ll say that the mechanics do feel much cheaper and clunkier here. Often upgrades are vague like “Increases damage by a bit” What’s a bit? I have no idea. But all the skills seem to lack the satisfying clearing of VS, making even the max level upgrades appear puny and dull. The difficulty is higher here, mostly because of a noticeable lack of sustain. The only way to heal HP is through the random heart-carrying enemies that seem to pop on screen every few minutes. This effectively turns the game into more of a bullet hell than Survivor-like. [h1] [b] Graphics (Quality/Technical) – [1/10] [/b] [/h1] Pretty bad, even when compared to VS. This is PS1-era fidelity. Animations are very simple. There is nothing about this game that looks good. UI is not great either. There are very few graphical options. Despite that, the game kept resetting my chosen options each time I started it up. I’ve had multiple times [i]during gameplay in the middle of a run[/i] where the game would minimize and show its weird little launcher. It makes me think this is some sort of malicious program or miner, but I have no proof, it could just simply be an awful technical side. 1440p @ 240hz | installed on SSD [h1] [b] Audio – [1/10] [/b] [/h1] Simple and generic. Music sounds very simple, like 8-bit. Also, the sound effects sound like they were recorded off of Discord using a mic. It’s bad. [h1] [b] Replay Factor (Longevity) – [6/10] [/b] [/h1] Decent, there’s the roguelite progression that is the same that VS has. If you can get past terrible everything else, there’s some good replay value here. [h1] [b] Final Verdict – [2/10] [/b] [/h1] Pizza Hero (PH) comes across initially as a Vampire Survivors-like game. It has most of the elements like the roguelite progression and borderline copyright infringement skills, but it’s lacking a major thing that VS has - defensive abilities, notably HP Regen. This small but simple change turns PH into more of a bullet hell than a true Survivor’s game. But PH digs the hole deeper than that. Between the clunky skills, terrible graphics/animations/UI, poor audio, and numerous technical issues, PH has a loot and feel of a game made during 48-hour game-a-thon event or a college capstone course. I understand that assessment can be a bit harsh, especially for an indie dev, so as someone who was given this game for free, would I have paid $2 for it? Probably not, no. I’d rather that money be put to Vampire Survivors and/or its DLC. So, I guess to be clear, I wouldn’t consider this game worth it in any world where Vampire Survivors already exists. I could understand if there was some passion behind this game, but there isn’t. It feels like abandonware that should be free. [h1] [b] Recommend? (Price) [Y/N] [/b] [/h1] [h1]No[/h1] This should really be free with an optional DLC for dev support. You can find my curator page here: https://steamcommunity.com/groups/Synik_GR
